# Playbook — implement an issue

You are stage 1 of the pipeline in `.github/AUTOMATION.md`. You turn one issue
into one reviewable pull request. A second Claude reviews your work, then a
human approves and merges. Optimise for **easy to review**, not for volume.

## 1. Understand before you touch anything

1. Read `CLAUDE.md`, then `SPEC.md`, then `DESIGN.md`. They outrank your
   instincts. Pay attention to the golden rules — money as integer cents,
   multi-tenant scoping plus RLS, server-side secrets, `quote_events`, validated
   AI output, mobile-first, loading/empty/error states on every screen.
2. Read the relevant skill in `.claude/skills/` before touching its area:
   `database` for schema or queries, `supabase-quotepilot` for auth, RLS,
   storage or the public quote page, `ui-design` for any screen work.
3. Read the issue and every comment on it. Then read the code it concerns —
   never patch from the issue text alone.

## 2. Decide whether to proceed

Stop and **do not open a pull request** if any of these hold:

- The issue is too vague to implement without guessing at product behaviour.
- It would take more than roughly 400 changed lines, or spans several
  unrelated areas — it needs splitting first.
- It asks for work from a later phase than the one the project is on
  (`SPEC.md` §14), or contradicts `SPEC.md` or `DESIGN.md`.
- It touches billing charges, deletes user data, or changes an auth or RLS
  boundary in a way the issue does not spell out precisely.

In that case: comment on the issue with the **specific** questions or the
proposed split (not "please clarify"), add the `claude:needs-human` label, and
finish. That is a successful run.

## 3. Branch

```bash
git checkout -b claude/issue-<number>-<short-kebab-slug>
```

The `claude/` prefix is what the review stage watches for. Never work on `main`.

## 4. Implement

- Only what the issue asks. No drive-by refactors, no reformatting untouched
  files, no dependency bumps that the issue does not require.
- Follow the code-quality standards in `CLAUDE.md`: small single-purpose
  functions, Zod at every boundary, no `any` without a comment justifying it,
  no magic strings (they belong in `lib/constants.ts`), external services only
  through their `lib/` wrapper, files under ~200 lines.
- Add tests where `CLAUDE.md` requires them: money math, AI parsing, and the
  accept-quote flow. Tests live next to the code as `*.test.ts`.
- Never commit secrets, `.env*` files, or a `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable holding
  anything sensitive.

## 5. Verify — all four must pass before you commit

```bash
npm run format      # writes; run it before format:check
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

If you cannot get them green, do not open a pull request claiming success. Push
what you have as a **draft** PR and say plainly in the description what is
failing and why.

## 6. Commit

One commit per logical step, present tense, explaining the why:

```
feat(quotes): record quote_events on accept

Closes #123

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

## 7. Open the pull request

```bash
git push -u origin claude/issue-<number>-<slug>
gh pr create --fill-first --base main
```

Fill in `.github/pull_request_template.md` properly:

- **What and why**, in a sentence or two a reviewer can check against the issue.
- `Closes #<number>` so the issue closes on merge.
- The **verification steps** — the exact commands you ran and, for UI work, how
  to check it on a phone-width viewport.
- Anything you deliberately left out, and any decision you were unsure about.
  Flag those explicitly; they are what the reviewer should look at hardest.

Do not add reviewers and do not merge. Labelling and the review happen
automatically.

## 8. House style for anything you post on GitHub

End every issue comment, PR description and review reply with:

```

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
```
